title: secp256k1-ecdlp: parallel Pollard rho on order-6 classes with a sigma walk, all arithmetic in instructions

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and input Q=[x]P on secp256k1 (fixed standard generator P), the parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39. It walks on the order-6 classes {±1, ±λ, ±λ²} with 2^32 walks and 2^16 adders, using batched affine additions. Walks run in trails from fresh coins, each ending at its first distinguished point, which it records once with its coins. The first key match is resolved by replaying both trails, so a degenerate match has probability exactly 1/r (Lemmas R and D). A fruitless cycle escapes to twice the canonical point of its least-key member, a doubling with no table. A repeated class within a trail is a short closure (length at most 64, detected and escaped within the per-entry bound, Lemmas E1* and E2), a closure of length 65 or more (Lemma F, DELTA_LONG below 2^-234), or an accidental equality bounded by DELTA_LOOP (section 3). Escape depth is controlled by the exact certificate of section 2.4 (no k below 2^56 with 2^k in Gamma, computed with m = 2^28) and by the depth tail DELTA_DEPTH (section 2.3). Abandonment is bounded in Lemma T'' (section 5). The 2-cycle excess is an exact forced-return identity (Lemma FR, section 4); its premise L-ori, that the non-equal share is 1/6, is measured at A = 8, 64, 256 and 1024 (evidence/sign-law.json). Total computation is at most 2^126.479214 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, distinguished-point storage and lookup, failures and restarts, collision replay, verification and output: 821 instructions per walk step on the common path plus a Markov reserve of 7.89 for rare work, that is 828.89 instructions per walk step at C = 1000. Rare work is charged at forced-path maxima, and the meter aborts with probability at most 1/64. Peak memory is at most 2^75.749960 bytes. Preprocessing, 2^47.131242 units, is included. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack on one target. The success bound 0.395898 is the model bound 0.411524, less 1/64 for the meter, less DELTA_CUT (about 1.1e-16), less DELTA_ABANDON (2.8e-14), less 2^-20. The probability is over x and the algorithm's coins. It relies on the premises in proof.md: M1 with the coupling of section 2.2 (fresh classes receive uniform, independent keys and orientations, uniform over every prefix), L-ori, H1 (random mapping, for the collision statistics of section 7), and H3 (the measured common-path counts are representative). The table and the coins come from the operating system, which is a property of the specification. The toy-curve runs and the small-build formal test support these premises; they do not prove them. This is a carefully accounted generic attack, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the procedure of proof.md section 1.3 on random prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3+7 (b=7) or y^2=x^3+4 (b=4) at budget tau = tau_e4/10^4, with fresh-coin trails and escapes to twice the canonical least-key point. The first key match is resolved by replaying both trails (Lemma R); a degenerate match fails. With check_all_replays every recorded trail is replayed and any replay that misses its record is counted. Reports the success rate against 1-exp(-tau), degenerate matches and replay mismatches. No oracle collision table. Toy scale only.
Check Lemma 1 of proof.md on random and edge-case reduced values, and the canonical-rotation rule against the exact minimum, with the exact fallback.
Recompute the claimed time_log2, preprocessing, memory and success lower bound from the stated parameters with exact integer arithmetic.
